text:
"Resolve GitHub issue #501: [BUG] participant transfer issue
Issue URL: https://github.com/IshaFoundationIT/prs-backend/issues/501

Issue body:
In the group registration, when we try participant transfer for a single participant, the whole group is getting cancelled.
And one target participant record is getting confirmed. In the target participant record, the SO is not getting created for zero transaction.

── READ THIS BEFORE YOU START ──
First, read your operating instructions: open and read
/home/dev/workspace/AGENT_CONTEXT.md and /home/dev/workspace/repo/AGENT.md
(if it exists) in your cwd. They contain the project system prompt, the
commit/push/PR mandate, the browser guidance, and the env layout
(Odoo on 127.0.0.1:18069, repo at /home/dev/workspace/repo). Do NOT skip
this and do NOT rely solely on the superpowers brainstorming checklist --
that checklist ends at \"transition to implementation\" and does NOT include
finishing the branch, so the finish steps below are part of YOUR task.

── WORKFLOW (do every step; do not stop early) ──
1. Understand the issue and explore the codebase (read before you write).
2. Make the smallest correct change in the addons repo.
3. Reload + upgrade Odoo: `docker restart env-odoo` then
   `docker exec env-odoo odoo -d odoo -u <addon> --stop-after-init`.
4. VERIFY VISUALLY with headless Chrome for Testing (do NOT launch a
   GUI browser). Two wrappers are on PATH and you MUST use them (raw
   `chrome --headless=new ...` hangs forever in this workspace: an empty
   DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS makes Chrome block on a D-Bus connection,
   and Odoo's /web/login redirect chain never fires a load event so
   Chrome waits indefinitely). The wrappers fix both:
     chrome-dom http://127.0.0.1:18069/web/login        # render page -> HTML on stdout
     chrome-shot /home/dev/workspace/repo/docs/issue-#501-after.png                http://127.0.0.1:18069/<your-route>              # capture a PNG screenshot
   (full-page/tall: append `--window-size=1280,2400` as a trailing flag.)
   Save the screenshot under the repo (e.g.
   /home/dev/workspace/repo/docs/issue-#501-after.png) and
   reference its path in the PR body. If the change has no UI surface
   (pure model/data change), say so explicitly in your final summary
   instead of silently skipping the screenshot.
5. FINISH — commit, push, and open a PR. This is mandatory and is the
   last step; do not stop after verifying:
     a. Commit on a NEW branch (do not commit directly to uat).
     b. Push the branch: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
     c. Open a pull request:
          gh pr create --base uat \
            --title \"<short summary>\" \
            --body \"<summary of the change + Resolves #501 + note the screenshot path>\"
     The `gh` CLI is installed and GH_TOKEN is in your environment. Push
     FIRST, then create the PR. Do NOT stop until the PR is created. Do
     NOT submit/merge the PR yourself.
If you cannot push or create the PR (auth failure, gh missing, etc.),
say so EXPLICITLY in your final summary — do NOT silently leave changes
uncommitted or unpushed."

137: dynamic forms, payments, and inventory. ~64 model files; the biggest are
138: `event_registration.py` (~3300 lines) and `event_flow.py` (~1900 lines).
139: 
140: ### Domain model graph (the entities you will touch)
141: 
142: - **`event.event`** — central. Inherits `cache.mixin`, `access.control.mixin`,
143:   `mail.thread`, `display.name.mixin`. User-facing date/time fields
144:   (`start_date`/`end_date`/`start_time`/`end_time` floats) compute the
145:   technical UTC `date_begin`/`date_end`. Has `financial_entity_id` ->
146:   `financial.entity`; ERP-enablement is derived from the entity code being in
147:   the `prs.erp_enabled_entities` config param (default `IF`).
148: - **`event.registration`** (model `event.registration`, mixin
149:   `event.registration.mixin`) — a participant's registration for an event;
150:   the largest model. Links `event_id`, `flow_id` (`event.flow`),
151:   `inventory_id` (`event.inventory`), `coupon_id`, `submission_id`
152:   (`form.submission`). Drives sale-order creation (`sale.order`/`sale.order.line`
153:   are extended here), cancellations (`event.registration_cancellation`), and
154:   transfers (`event.registration.transfer`).
155: - **`event.flow`** / **`event.flow.step`** — the participant flow for an event.
156:   `event.flow` has `flow_step_ids`; `event.flow_step` has `form_id`
157:   (`form.form`), self-referential `next_step_id`, and
158:   `block_config_ids` (`event.reg.block.config`). Flow definitions are
159:   templated via `flow.definition`.
160: - **Form engine** — `form.form` -> `form.page` -> `form.section` -> `form.field`
161:   -> `form.field.choice` (+ `form.field.validation`,
162:   `form.display.condition`). A `form.submission` captures participant data.
163:   Template versions live as `tmpl.form.*`. Fields have a master
164:   (`form.field.master`) and several mixins; display conditions drive
165:   conditional field visibility.
166: - **`event.inventory`** — what's offered for an event (base/combo), with
167:   `pricing_type` (`program_fee`/`donation`/...). **ERP product validation**
168:   (see `ERP_PRODUCT_IMPLEMENTATION_CHANGE_SUMMARY.md`): for ERP-enabled events,
169:   `type='base'` + `pricing_type='program_fee'` inventory must have a
170:   `product_id` whose `default_code` is set; combo headers are skipped but
171:   their linked `base_ids` are validated; `donation` is exempt.
172: - **`financial.entity`** — entity (e.g. `IF`); its fee products
173:   (`adjustment_product_id`/`rereg_product_id`/`cancellation_product_id`) must
174:   have `default_code` when the entity is ERP-enabled.
175: - **Payments** — `payment.transaction`, `payment.installment`,
176:   `prs.refund.queue`; the `isha_payment` addon provides payment primitives.
177: - **SSO / auth** — `isha_sso_auth_generic` provides SSO; `res.users` is
178:   extended; `rbac` / `rbac.privilege` provide role-based access control layered
179:   on `access.control.mixin`.
180: - **Portal / website** — `prs/controllers/main.py` exposes
181:   `/prs/form-preview/`. The `irs_website*` addons provide the public-facing
182:   site; `irs_appointment*` add appointment booking (Google Calendar sync).
183: 
184: ### Supporting custom addons (all under `custom_addons/`)
185: 
186: - `isha_base` — shared base (webhook push utils to Slack/Google Space, etc.).
187: - `isha_payment` — payment primitives.
188: - `isha_sso_auth_generic` — SSO auth (depends `auth_oauth`).
189: - `call_campaign` — call campaigns.
190: - `program_schedule` — program scheduling (depends `prs`).
191: - `rbac` — role-based access control (depends `prs`).
192: - `irs_appointment` / `irs_appointment_google_calendar` — appointments +
193:   Google Calendar sync (depend `prs`).
194: - `irs_web_*`, `irs_website*` — web/website extensions.
195: - `auto_translate_fields`, `base_whatsapp`, `image_preview_zoom`,
196:   `web_responsive`, `sentry`, `access_control_extension` — utilities.
197: 
198: ### Conventions you must follow
199: 
200: - **Python style** — Odoo 17 ORM patterns. Models use `cache.mixin` and
201:   `access.control.mixin` widely; both override `create`/`write` and (in
202:   `cache.mixin`) call `cr.commit()`. **This breaks `TransactionCase`
203:   savepoints** — tests that touch cached models stub out `cr.commit` in
204:   `setUp` (see `prs/tests/test_erp_product_validation.py` for the canonical
205:   pattern: `self.env.cr.commit = lambda: None` + `addCleanup` to restore it).
206:   Use `TransactionCase` (not `SavepointCase`) and replicate that stub when your
207:   test creates/updates cached models.
208: - **Tests** — `prs/tests/` has ~26 test modules, `@tagged(...)` per area. Add
209:   tests for any model change; import new test modules in `prs/tests/__init__.py`.
210: - **Views/security** — views live in `prs/views/*_views.xml`; ACLs in
211:   `security/ir.model.access.csv` + `security/prs_security.xml`. Data/cron/mail
212:   templates in `prs/data/`. New model files must be imported in
213:   `prs/models/__init__.py` and listed in `prs/__manifest__.py` `data`/`demo`.
214: - **Config params** — runtime config via `ir.config_parameter`; defaults
215:   seeded in `prs/data/ir_config_parameter.xml` (e.g.
216:   `prs.erp_enabled_entities`). Read with
217:   `self.env['ir.config_parameter'].sudo().get_param(key)`.
218: - **i18n** — wrap user-facing strings in `_()`.
219: - **External integrations** — Sentry (`sentry_sdk`), Celery, Redis, Google
220:   Gemini (`google-genai`), S3 (`boto3`), Google Translate (`googletrans`),
221:   Kafka (certs in `etc/assets/certificates/kafka/`). These need config keys
222:   (see the profile's `required_config_keys`); in this masked env many are
223:   stubbed/unset, so guard integration code paths.
224: - **Undeclared python deps** — `Levenshtein`, `boto3`, `celery`, `fuzzywuzzy`,
225:   `imgkit`, `jmespath`, `name_match_engine`, `phonenumbers`, `pyqrcode`,
226:   `sentry_sdk` are used but not always in a manifest's requirements; they are
227:   installed in the env image. `requirements.txt` files live in
228:   `custom_addons/{sentry,isha_base,prs,auto_translate_fields}/requirements.txt`.
229: 
230: ### How to run / verify
231: 
232: - The Odoo instance is already running with the masked DB and the `prs` module
233:   installed. After a code change: `docker restart env-odoo`, then for an addon
234:   upgrade `docker exec env-odoo odoo -d odoo -u prs --stop-after-init` (or the
235:   specific submodule).
236: - Run a single test tag: `docker exec env-odoo odoo -d odoo --test-tags
237:   /prs:TestErpProductValidation --stop-after-init` (odoo must be started with
238:   `--test-enable` / `--init` for the module to load tests; the env image is
239:   configured for this).
240: - Verify the UI loads: `obscura fetch http://127.0.0.1:18069/web/login --dump
241:   text` should return the login page.
242: 
243: ## Your task
244: 
245: Read the `## GitHub issue` and `## Task` sections in
246: `/home/dev/workspace/AGENT_CONTEXT.md` (next to your cwd) for the specific
247: work. Make the smallest correct change consistent with the conventions above,
248: add/adjust tests, verify Odoo still serves `/web/login` (obscura), and commit
249: + push to a branch as described above. The DB data is masked/fake — safe to
250: mutate freely.

(End of file - total 250 lines)

105: - Wait for dynamic content: `obscura fetch <url> --wait-until networkidle0`
106: - CDP server (Puppeteer/Playwright): `obscura serve --port 9222` then connect
107:   to `ws://127.0.0.1:9222`
108: 
109: Keep `obscura` and `obscura-worker` in the same directory (they already are on
110: the AMI). Obscura is a lightweight headless browser engine — fast, low-memory,
111: no Chrome/Node dependency.
112: 
113: ## Git — you MUST commit and push your work
114: 
115: CRITICAL. Your changes are worthless if they stay only in this env's working
116: tree. When the task is done:
117: 
118: 1. Commit on a **new branch** (do not commit directly to `uat`). Use
119:    superpowers' `using-git-worktrees` / `finishing-a-development-branch` skills.
120: 2. **Push** the branch: `git push -u origin <branch>`. The env has git
121:    credentials (Coder SSH key for SSH URLs; a token for HTTPS URLs) so pushes
122:    work without extra setup.
123: 3. **Open a pull request** with `gh pr create --base uat` (the `gh` CLI is
124:    installed and `GH_TOKEN` is in your environment — same token as the git
125:    push). Push first, then create the PR against `uat`. Use `--title` and
126:    `--body` with a clear summary + "Resolves #N". If `gh` is unavailable or
127:    `GH_TOKEN` is unset, say so explicitly in your final summary — do NOT
128:    silently skip the PR.
129: 
130: If you cannot push (auth failure, etc.), say so explicitly in your final
131: summary — do NOT silently leave changes uncommitted.
132: 
133: ## Codebase orientation — PRS (Program Registration System)
134: 
135: The core app is the **`prs`** custom addon (`custom_addons/prs/`), an Odoo 17
136: `application` module. It models programs/events, their registration flow,
137: dynamic forms, payments, and inventory. ~64 model files; the biggest are
138: `event_registration.py` (~3300 lines) and `event_flow.py` (~1900 lines).
139: 
140: ### Domain model graph (the entities you will touch)
141: 
142: - **`event.event`** — central. Inherits `cache.mixin`, `access.control.mixin`,
143:   `mail.thread`, `display.name.mixin`. User-facing date/time fields
144:   (`start_date`/`end_date`/`start_time`/`end_time` floats) compute the
145:   technical UTC `date_begin`/`date_end`. Has `financial_entity_id` ->
146:   `financial.entity`; ERP-enablement is derived from the entity code being in
147:   the `prs.erp_enabled_entities` config param (default `IF`).
148: - **`event.registration`** (model `event.registration`, mixin
149:   `event.registration.mixin`) — a participant's registration for an event;
150:   the largest model. Links `event_id`, `flow_id` (`event.flow`),
151:   `inventory_id` (`event.inventory`), `coupon_id`, `submission_id`
152:   (`form.submission`). Drives sale-order creation (`sale.order`/`sale.order.line`
153:   are extended here), cancellations (`event.registration_cancellation`), and
154:   transfers (`event.registration.transfer`).
155: - **`event.flow`** / **`event.flow.step`** — the participant flow for an event.
156:   `event.flow` has `flow_step_ids`; `event.flow_step` has `form_id`
157:   (`form.form`), self-referential `next_step_id`, and
158:   `block_config_ids` (`event.reg.block.config`). Flow definitions are
159:   templated via `flow.definition`.
160: - **Form engine** — `form.form` -> `form.page` -> `form.section` -> `form.field`
161:   -> `form.field.choice` (+ `form.field.validation`,
162:   `form.display.condition`). A `form.submission` captures participant data.
163:   Template versions live as `tmpl.form.*`. Fields have a master
164:   (`form.field.master`) and several mixins; display conditions drive
165:   conditional field visibility.
166: - **`event.inventory`** — what's offered for an event (base/combo), with
167:   `pricing_type` (`program_fee`/`donation`/...). **ERP product validation**
168:   (see `ERP_PRODUCT_IMPLEMENTATION_CHANGE_SUMMARY.md`): for ERP-enabled events,
169:   `type='base'` + `pricing_type='program_fee'` inventory must have a
170:   `product_id` whose `default_code` is set; combo headers are skipped but
171:   their linked `base_ids` are validated; `donation` is exempt.
172: - **`financial.entity`** — entity (e.g. `IF`); its fee products
173:   (`adjustment_product_id`/`rereg_product_id`/`cancellation_product_id`) must
174:   have `default_code` when the entity is ERP-enabled.
175: - **Payments** — `payment.transaction`, `payment.installment`,
176:   `prs.refund.queue`; the `isha_payment` addon provides payment primitives.
177: - **SSO / auth** — `isha_sso_auth_generic` provides SSO; `res.users` is
178:   extended; `rbac` / `rbac.privilege` provide role-based access control layered
179:   on `access.control.mixin`.
180: - **Portal / website** — `prs/controllers/main.py` exposes
181:   `/prs/form-preview/`. The `irs_website*` addons provide the public-facing
182:   site; `irs_appointment*` add appointment booking (Google Calendar sync).
183: 
184: ### Supporting custom addons (all under `custom_addons/`)
185: 
186: - `isha_base` — shared base (webhook push utils to Slack/Google Space, etc.).
187: - `isha_payment` — payment primitives.
188: - `isha_sso_auth_generic` — SSO auth (depends `auth_oauth`).
189: - `call_campaign` — call campaigns.
190: - `program_schedule` — program scheduling (depends `prs`).
191: - `rbac` — role-based access control (depends `prs`).
192: - `irs_appointment` / `irs_appointment_google_calendar` — appointments +
193:   Google Calendar sync (depend `prs`).
194: - `irs_web_*`, `irs_website*` — web/website extensions.
195: - `auto_translate_fields`, `base_whatsapp`, `image_preview_zoom`,
196:   `web_responsive`, `sentry`, `access_control_extension` — utilities.
197: 
198: ### Conventions you must follow
199: 
200: - **Python style** — Odoo 17 ORM patterns. Models use `cache.mixin` and
201:   `access.control.mixin` widely; both override `create`/`write` and (in
202:   `cache.mixin`) call `cr.commit()`. **This breaks `TransactionCase`
203:   savepoints** — tests that touch cached models stub out `cr.commit` in
204:   `setUp` (see `prs/tests/test_erp_product_validation.py` for the canonical
205:   pattern: `self.env.cr.commit = lambda: None` + `addCleanup` to restore it).
206:   Use `TransactionCase` (not `SavepointCase`) and replicate that stub when your
207:   test creates/updates cached models.
208: - **Tests** — `prs/tests/` has ~26 test modules, `@tagged(...)` per area. Add
209:   tests for any model change; import new test modules in `prs/tests/__init__.py`.
210: - **Views/security** — views live in `prs/views/*_views.xml`; ACLs in
211:   `security/ir.model.access.csv` + `security/prs_security.xml`. Data/cron/mail
212:   templates in `prs/data/`. New model files must be imported in
213:   `prs/models/__init__.py` and listed in `prs/__manifest__.py` `data`/`demo`.
214: - **Config params** — runtime config via `ir.config_parameter`; defaults
215:   seeded in `prs/data/ir_config_parameter.xml` (e.g.
216:   `prs.erp_enabled_entities`). Read with
217:   `self.env['ir.config_parameter'].sudo().get_param(key)`.
218: - **i18n** — wrap user-facing strings in `_()`.
219: - **External integrations** — Sentry (`sentry_sdk`), Celery, Redis, Google
220:   Gemini (`google-genai`), S3 (`boto3`), Google Translate (`googletrans`),
221:   Kafka (certs in `etc/assets/certificates/kafka/`). These need config keys
222:   (see the profile's `required_config_keys`); in this masked env many are
223:   stubbed/unset, so guard integration code paths.
224: - **Undeclared python deps** — `Levenshtein`, `boto3`, `celery`, `fuzzywuzzy`,
225:   `imgkit`, `jmespath`, `name_match_engine`, `phonenumbers`, `pyqrcode`,
226:   `sentry_sdk` are used but not always in a manifest's requirements; they are
227:   installed in the env image. `requirements.txt` files live in
228:   `custom_addons/{sentry,isha_base,prs,auto_translate_fields}/requirements.txt`.
229: 
230: ### How to run / verify
231: 
232: - The Odoo instance is already running with the masked DB and the `prs` module
233:   installed. After a code change: `docker restart env-odoo`, then for an addon
234:   upgrade `docker exec env-odoo odoo -d odoo -u prs --stop-after-init` (or the
235:   specific submodule).
236: - Run a single test tag: `docker exec env-odoo odoo -d odoo --test-tags
237:   /prs:TestErpProductValidation --stop-after-init` (odoo must be started with
238:   `--test-enable` / `--init` for the module to load tests; the env image is
239:   configured for this).
240: - Verify the UI loads: `obscura fetch http://127.0.0.1:18069/web/login --dump
241:   text` should return the login page.
242: 
243: ## Your task
244: 
245: Read the `## GitHub issue` and `## Task` sections in
246: `/home/dev/workspace/AGENT_CONTEXT.md` (next to your cwd) for the specific

249: + push to a branch as described above. The DB data is masked/fake — safe to

<skill_content name="systematic-debugging">
# Skill: systematic-debugging

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

Random fixes waste time and create new bugs. Quick patches mask underlying issues.

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

**Related skills:**
- **superpowers:test-driven-development** - For creating failing test case (Phase 4, Step 1)
- **superpowers:verification-before-completion** - Verify fix worked before claiming success

## Real-World Impact

From debugging sessions:
- Systematic approach: 15-30 minutes to fix
- Random fixes approach: 2-3 hours of thrashing
- First-time fix rate: 95% vs 40%
- New bugs introduced: Near zero vs common

Base directory for this skill: /opt/superpowers/skills/systematic-debugging
Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.

The actual transfer orchestration happens in the **facade** (external service). When the facade transfers a single participant in a group:
1. It creates a new registration with the target booking_token and `type='PARTICIPANT_TRANSFER'`
2. It cancels the SOURCE registration (`source_registration_id`)

Since all group registrations share the same `booking_token`, and the source registration is shared (each target has its own `source_registration_id`), the cancel of one source registration should only affect that one source registration. However, if the facade **cancels the entire source booking** (all registrations sharing the source booking_token), that would cancel the WHOLE group.

The key question is: does the facade cancel the individual source registration, or does it cancel the entire source booking (all siblings)? The Odoo code cannot prevent either since `_local_cancel_unpaid` only writes `state='cancel'` on the single registration passed to it.

205:     def _find_clubbable_l1(self, reg_rec, line_item, product_id, line_name,
206:                            price_unit, discount_percentage):
207:         """Return an existing L1 on this SO that ``reg_rec``'s primary line can be
208:         merged into (qty-incremented), or an empty recordset for a discrete line.
209: 
210:         Clubbing collapses identical primary lines of a group into one qty=N
211:         line. Rules:
212: 
213:         - Never merge into an adjustment line (``is_l1`` only) and never merge
214:           rows whose price/discount/name differ.
215:         - A fresh ``new`` row merges only with other new rows (no source
216:           registration on either side).
217:         - A chain row (upgrade / event-transfer / participant-transfer /
218:           downgrade) merges only within a UNIFORM cohort: the candidate's
219:           registration is the same ``reg.type``, targets the same event, and has
220:           the same source-delivered state. That state governs the parent
221:           ``reduce_aq_qty``, the L2 ``active_ordered_qty`` and the invoicing
222:           markers built in event_registration._create_sale_order_lines, so
223:           mixing states on one line would be inconsistent.
224: 
225:         The new-vs-chain split is enforced via the candidate's linked
226:         registration (not by excluding adjustment-referenced L1s): a chain L1 is
227:         already referenced by its own L2 by the time the next sibling is built,
228:         so an id-exclusion would wrongly block chain self-clubbing.
229:         """
230:         SOL = self.env['sale.order.line'].sudo()
231:         so = reg_rec.sale_order_id
232:         if not so:
233:             return SOL
234: 
235:         row_kind = (line_item or {}).get('row_kind') or 'new'
236:         source_reg = reg_rec.source_registration_id
237:         # A new row must have no source; a chain row must have one. Reject any
238:         # mismatch (defensive -- keeps clubbing out of malformed rows).
239:         if bool(source_reg) != (row_kind != 'new'):
240:             return SOL
241: 
242:         candidates = SOL.search([
243:             ('order_id', '=', so.id),
244:             ('product_id', '=', product_id),
245:             ('is_l1', '=', True),
246:             ('name', '=', line_name),
247:         ])
248:         if not candidates:
249:             return SOL
250: 
251:         price_dig = self.env['decimal.precision'].precision_get('Product Price')
252:         disc_dig = self.env['decimal.precision'].precision_get('Discount')
253:         src_delivered = (
254:             bool(source_reg.sale_order_line_id.qty_delivered)
255:             if source_reg else False
256:         )
257: 
258:         for cand in candidates:
259:             if float_compare(cand.price_unit, price_unit,
260:                              precision_digits=price_dig) != 0:
261:                 continue
262:             if float_compare(cand.discount, discount_percentage,
263:                              precision_digits=disc_dig) != 0:
264:                 continue
265:             cand_reg = cand.registration_ids[:1]
266:             if not cand_reg:

269:             if bool(cand_reg.source_registration_id) != bool(source_reg):

271:             if source_reg:
272:                 # Chain cohort uniformity.
273:                 if cand_reg.type != reg_rec.type:

275:                 if cand_reg.event_id != reg_rec.event_id:

279:                 )
280:                 if cand_src_delivered != src_delivered:
281:                     continue
282:             return cand

### 2. Model: `event.transfer.policy` (New Multi-Tier Transfer Policy)

**File:** `/home/dev/workspace/repo/custom_addons/prs/models/event_transfer_policy.py` (293 lines)

This is the **new** multi-tier transfer policy model replacing the legacy one. Supports sliding-scale policies evaluated in `sequence` order (first match wins).

- **`_name`**: `event.transfer.policy` (line 25)
- **Policy kinds** (line 39-44):
  - `program_transfer` - Registration moved to a DIFFERENT event/program
  - `participant_transfer` - Registration handed to ANOTHER PERSON, same event

  - `_check_ppt_transfer_pricing()` - participant_transfer CANNOT use `pay_pct_of_target`

### 4. Transfer-Related Fields/Methods on `event.registration`

**File:** `/home/dev/workspace/repo/custom_addons/prs/models/event_registration.py` (3326 lines)

#### 4a. Transfer Type Constants (lines 57-66)

```python

    'PARTICIPANT_TRANSFER': 'Participant Transfer',
    'PARTICIPANT_TRANSFERRED': 'Participant Transferred (source)',
    'EVENT_TRANSFER': 'Event Transfer',
    'EVENT_TRANSFERRED': 'Event Transferred (source)',
```

#### 4b. `type` field (line 148)
- `type = fields.Char(string="Type", tracking=True)` - Char (not Selection) for legacy compatibility

#### 4c. `source_registration_id` / `target_registration_id` (lines 1064-1080)

- **`source_registration_id`** (line 1064): Many2one to `event.registration` - links a transfer/upgrade target back to its source
- **`target_registration_id`** (line 1068-1071): Computed field - finds latest non-cancelled child reg where `source_registration_id = self.id`
- **`_compute_target_registration_id()`** (lines 1073-1080): Searches for child registrations and returns the latest non-cancelled one
- **`action_open_source_registration()`** (lines 1082-1097): UI action to navigate to source registration
- **`action_open_target_registration()`** (lines 1099-1114): UI action to navigate to target registration

#### 4d. `action_cancel()` (lines 1215-1236) - **Blocks paid registrations from local cancel**

Paid records (completed payment transactions or transfer-chain ancestors) are **blocked** from local cancellation. They must go through the refund/transfer flow. Key logic:
```python
if self._has_confirmed_payment():
    raise UserError(_(
        "This registration has a confirmed payment and cannot be "
        "cancelled from here. Paid registrations must be cancelled "
        "through the refund or transfer flow so the policy and "
        "refund are recorded correctly."
    ))
```

#### 4e. `_has_confirmed_payment()` (lines 1277-1319) - **Transfer-chain-aware payment check**

This is the **single source of truth** for whether a registration is "paid". It accounts for transfers:
- **`v_completed` state** (line 1286-1287): covers inbound transfers (target gets VIR-IN-* payment_transaction)
- **`amount > 0` filter** (line 1288-1289): excludes negative VIR-OUT-* rows on transfer-out source
- **`linked_payment_txns`** (lines 1290-1291, 1310-1318): covers transfer-chain ancestors referenced via `reg_data_properties.linked_payment_txns`

---

### 5. Sale Order Creation During Transfers

#### 5a. `_create_sale_order_by_transaction()` (lines 2049-2262)

The main SO creation method called from the cron. Key transfer-related logic:

**Lines 2119-2134 - Zero-amount transfer handling:**
```python
is_zero_amount_txn = (
    not transaction.amount
    or (transaction.reference or "").upper().startswith("ZERO")
)
```
A 0-amount transfer / 0-delta upgrade / complimentary row is materialised from a synthetic "ZERO-{booking_token}" payment transaction. Its own e-receipt is suppressed; only the parent SO's values carry forward.

**Lines 2176-2188 - Free participant transfer billing:**
```python
# Free participant transfer: billing comes from the source SO
if not (
    first_reg.type == 'PARTICIPANT_TRANSFER'
    and first_reg.payment_status == 'free'
):
    sale_order_data.update(
        first_reg.get_billing_partner_data_from_stored_request(transaction=transaction)
    )
```
For free participant transfers, billing data is NOT taken from the new request but is copied from the source SO via `_populate_billing_from_parent`.

96:         """Build the L1 (primary) sale-order line for a registration.
97: 
98:         line_item (Phase 0+): per-registration pricing dict from
99:         payment_line_items_json. Required keys when present:
100:           price_unit, charged_amount, row_kind, source_credit
101:         Optional:
102:           discount_type ('percentage'|'flat_fee'|None), discount_value,
103:           discount_amount, discount_source
104: 
105:         When line_item is provided, an identical sibling primary line on the
106:         same SO is qty-incremented instead of duplicated ("clubbing", see
107:         _find_clubbable_l1):
108: 
109:         - Fresh ``row_kind == 'new'`` rows club with other new rows that share
110:           product + name + price_unit + discount.
111:         - Chain rows (upgrade / event-transfer / participant-transfer /
112:           downgrade) club only with siblings of the SAME cohort: same target
113:           event, same ``reg.type`` and the same source-delivered state -- so the
114:           parent reduction, L2 ``active_ordered_qty`` and invoicing markers built
115:           in event_registration._create_sale_order_lines stay uniform.
116: 
117:         Clubbing never merges into an adjustment line and never merges rows with
118:         a different price/discount, so per-cohort totals are preserved.

```python
def _create_sale_order_for_free_transfer(self, booking_token):
    EventRegistrationSudo = self.env['event.registration'].sudo()
    SaleOrder = self.env['sale.order'].sudo()

    registrations = EventRegistrationSudo.search([
        ('booking_token', '=', booking_token),
        ('source_registration_id.sale_order_id', '!=', False),
        ('sale_order_id', '=', False),
    ], order='id asc')

    if not registrations:
        _logger.warning(f'No event registrations found for given booking token {booking_token}')
        return False

    first_reg = registrations[0]
    src_reg_sale_order_id = first_reg.source_registration_id.sale_order_id
    event_properties = first_reg.event_id.event_properties or {}
    sale_order_data = {
        'state': 'sale',
        'currency_id': src_reg_sale_order_id.currency_id.id,
        'financial_entity': first_reg.event_id.financial_entity_id.name,
        'entity': first_reg.event_id.entity,
        'tally_program_code': event_properties.get('tally_program_code'),
        'date_order': src_reg_sale_order_id.date_order,
        'client_order_ref': src_reg_sale_order_id.client_order_ref,
        'receipt_numbers': src_reg_sale_order_id.receipt_numbers,
        'payment_gateway_config': src_reg_sale_order_id.payment_gateway_config.id if src_reg_sale_order_id.payment_gateway_config else None,
        'parent_sale_order_id': src_reg_sale_order_id.id,
    }
    sale_order_data.update(first_reg.get_billing_partner_data())
    sale_order = SaleOrder.create(sale_order_data)
    self._populate_billing_from_parent(sale_order)
    sale_order.is_ready_for_sync = self._compute_is_ready_for_sync(
        sale_order, ereceipt_number=None, free_transfer=True,
    )
    if not sale_order.is_ready_for_sync:
        _logger.info(
            f'is_ready_for_sync=False on free-transfer SO {sale_order.id} '
            f'(booking {booking_token}): billing incomplete after parent fallback'
        )

    registrations.write({
        'sale_order_id': sale_order.id
    })

    for reg in registrations:
        reg._create_sale_order_lines()

    sale_order.order_line._recompute_invoicing_start_datetime_after_sol_link()
    return sale_order
```

**Search criteria:** Finds ALL registrations sharing the same `booking_token` that (a) have a `source_registration_id.sale_order_id` (i.e., are transfer targets with a paid source), and (b) do NOT yet have a `sale_order_id`. It creates ONE shared SO for all of them.

**Group booking handling:** YES, this handles group bookings implicitly. All registrations sharing a `booking_token` are found, one SO is created, and then `_create_sale_order_lines()` is called for EACH registration individually. The `_create_sale_order_lines()` method at line 2612 handles L1 clubbing via `_build_sale_order_line1()` (in isha_payment).

## Summary of Bug Root Causes

### Bug 1: Transferring a single participant cancels the WHOLE group

**Root cause:** The Odoo-side cancellation code (`action_cancel` at line 1215, `_local_cancel_unpaid` at line 1372) operates on `self.ensure_one()` - a single registration only. There is **no group-awareness in the cancel path**. The refund cron at line 3028 has a comment saying "group bookings cancel atomically (see prs partial-cancel invariant)" but this is only an assumed invariant, not enforced in code.

The actual transfer orchestration happens in the **facade** (external service). When the facade transfers a single participant in a group:
1. It creates a new registration with the target booking_token and `type='PARTICIPANT_TRANSFER'`
2. It cancels the SOURCE registration (`source_registration_id`)

Since all group registrations share the same `booking_token`, and the source registration is shared (each target has its own `source_registration_id`), the cancel of one source registration should only affect that one source registration. However, if the facade **cancels the entire source booking** (all registrations sharing the source booking_token), that would cancel the WHOLE group.

The key question is: does the facade cancel the individual source registration, or does it cancel the entire source booking (all siblings)? The Odoo code cannot prevent either since `_local_cancel_unpaid` only writes `state='cancel'` on the single registration passed to it.

### Bug 2: Target participant SO is not created for zero transactions

**Root cause:** The SO creation for free transfers depends on the registration being picked up by the cron's Branch B query (line 1813-1819):
```python
('type', '!=', False),
('sale_order_id', '=', False),
('source_registration_id.sale_order_id', '!=', False),
('payment_status', '=', 'free'),
('state', 'in', ['open', 'done']),
```

If a participant transfer has `payment_status` set to something other than `'free'` (e.g., `'paid'` or `'to_pay'`), it will NOT be picked up by Branch B. It would need a payment transaction for Branch A instead.

For zero-amount paid transfers, the facade injects a `ZERO-{booking_token}` transaction (amount=0), which IS picked up by Branch A via `__get_unprocessed_payment_transactions()`. But if the facade fails to inject this synthetic transaction, or if the transaction is in a wrong state, the SO will never be created.

Additionally, if the group's `source_registration_id.sale_order_id` is `False` (the source registration hasn't gotten its SO yet when the transfer is created), the search at line 1816 (`source_registration_id.sale_order_id', '!=', False`) would miss it. The cron would never pick it up again unless the source registration gets its SO later and the cron runs again.
